newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawmakers urge London to pass minorities bill.
newsitem.headline: HK lawmakers urge London to pass minorities bill.

text.p: Hong Kong legislators on Friday urged London to approve a bill granting British citizenship to the territory's ethnic minorities, who fear becoming stateless after the British colony reverts to China in July.
They made the call during a meeting with visiting British minister for Hong Kong, Jeremy Hanley.
"One of the issues that took up most of our time is the question of ethnic minorities," legislator Emily Lau told reporters. "We urge the British government to support the bill."
"The feelings are running very high. Everybody in Hong Kong is very concerned, including the Governor (Chris Patten). So we hope they would deal with that honourably," she added.
Lau quoted Hanley as saying the British government was still considering the issue.
But British Prime Minister John Major's government has opposed the bill, and without official backing it stands no chance of becoming law.
The bill, now going through the British parliament, would give full British citizenship to 8,000 residents of Hong Kong after it returns to China on July 1, after more than 150 years of British rule.

The 8,000, most of them of South Asian descent, say they would effectively be left stateless after the handover because Chinese citizenship is based on ethnic criteria and Britain is denying them full citizenship.
Instead, they are being offered the status of British overseas citizens or nationals, which allows them to travel on British-issued passports but gives them no right to live in Britain.
